main_body: farm building (barn with pitched roof and red wooden walls)
top_band: red-brown shingled roof slope from row 6 to row 57 (with a small chimney at rows 0-8 and a dormer in the middle)
evidence: Reading down a column on the main body (just off-center to avoid the central dormer): rows 6-55 are the pitched roof surface (shingled top band), rows 56-57 are a distinct lighter tan/orange front eave trim line, rows 58-61 are a dark eave shadow under the roof overhang, and rows 62-92 are the vertical front wall with recessed windows and barn doors, resting on a stone base.

style.evidence: While the roof has a decent repeating shingle pattern, the lower wall is composed of simple vertical stripes of two flat red tones without wood grain or speckle, and the white barn door framing and X-braces are completely flat single-colour fills with no shading steps. Compared to the Beodeul references (which have richly textured stone/plaster walls, multi-tone wood beams, and detailed roof tile highlights), the candidate's front wall and doors look flat, geometric, and much lower in information density.
